items.text: The cost of support that does not scale.
Ticket volume grows faster than headcount, and a chatbot with no real design behind it just adds another dead end for customers and employees to run into.
See how we fix this
01  Support that cannot keep up with demand
Peak periods and after-hours requests pile up faster than a human team can answer them, and every delay shows up as a lower satisfaction score.
02  Knowledge trapped in scattered systems
Answers live across wikis, ticketing tools, and spreadsheets that no single agent, human or bot, can search in one place.
03  Bots that escalate more than they resolve
A shallow keyword bot escalates almost everything it hears, so the team ends up supporting the bot instead of being helped by it.
04  No visibility into what is working
Without conversation analytics, there is no way to see where the bot succeeds, where it fails, or what to fix next.

items.text: What a well-built virtual agent supports, by industry.
The same design and integration approach adapts to how each sector’s support and service requests actually work. These are representative scenarios, each scoped to a defined set of intents.
Discuss your industry
Retail and e-commerce
Order status, returns, and product questions are resolved instantly, freeing the service team for the requests that need a person.
Financial services
Balance checks, transaction lookups, and routine requests are handled inside strict identity and compliance controls.
Healthcare
Appointment scheduling and routine patient questions are automated under role-based access and data residency requirements.
Manufacturing and field service
Technicians get instant answers on parts, procedures, and ticket status from a Teams bot, without leaving the tools they already use.

items.text: Power Virtual Agents at the center of the Microsoft ecosystem.
A bot is only as useful as the systems it can reach. Folio3 Azure positions Power Virtual Agents as the conversational layer across the Microsoft estate and the systems around it.
See integration options
Power Platform
Power Virtual Agents draws on Dataverse for data, Power Automate for action, and Power Apps for anything that needs a full interface, from one connected platform.
Microsoft Teams and Omnichannel
Bots deploy natively into Teams for internal use and into web and social channels for customers, from a single build.
Azure AI and Bot Framework
Deeper language understanding and custom logic extend the bot through Azure AI services and the Bot Framework SDK when a scenario needs it.

items.text: From first conversation to a production-ready agent.
Engagements begin with the requests people actually make today and move to a governed, measured bot in clear stages.
Start with a discovery workshop
01  Discover
Review ticket history and transcripts to identify the highest-volume, most resolvable intents, and define the scope for version one.
02  Design
Build the conversation flows, entities, and escalation paths for the prioritized topics, with fallback handled deliberately.
03  Build and integrate
Connect the bot to Dataverse, Power Automate, and line-of-business systems so it can look up and act on real data.
04  Deploy and optimize
Launch across the right channels, then tune topics and coverage from real conversation analytics.

items.text: Power Virtual Agents licensing, in plain terms.

Power Virtual Agents is licensed and metered through Microsoft, and cost depends on how much conversation volume runs through premium capacity. Folio3 Azure sizes this during discovery, so cost is understood before the build begins.
Get a capacity assessment
Message-based capacity
Sessions are metered by billed topics, and volume is estimated from real ticket history rather than guessed after launch.
Included entitlements
Many Power Apps and Power Automate licenses already include a baseline of Power Virtual Agents capacity. Folio3 Azure confirms what is already covered first.
Add-on capacity packs
Where volume exceeds included entitlements, capacity packs are sized to actual usage instead of purchased as a guess.

items.text: Where a well-built virtual agent pays back.
A properly scoped bot returns value in three areas. These are the factors to weigh when sizing the investment.
Estimate your ROI
Lower cost per interaction
Routine requests resolve without a human touch, so support cost per ticket drops as volume grows.
Faster resolution and higher CSAT
Instant answers to common requests cut wait time, and clean escalation keeps complex cases from getting stuck.
Freed-up human capacity
Agents and specialists spend their time on the requests that actually need judgment, not the ones a bot could have handled.

items.text: Frequently Asked Questions
What technology leaders ask before committing to Power Virtual Agents.

A basic FAQ bot matches keywords to static answers. Power Virtual Agents is built on real conversation flows, live data lookups through Power Automate and Dataverse, and clean escalation, so it can look up account details, complete actions, and hand off with context instead of only reciting text.

No. Power Virtual Agents can run on static topics alone, but connecting it to Power Automate and Dataverse is what lets it look up real data and complete actions instead of just describing them, and that connection is where most of the value comes from.

Timelines depend on how many intents are in scope and how many systems the bot needs to reach. A first version scoped to a handful of high-volume topics can launch in weeks; the full plan and scope are confirmed during discovery.

Power Virtual Agents is metered through Microsoft by conversation volume, with many Power Apps and Power Automate licenses already including a baseline entitlement. Folio3 Azure sizes actual usage during discovery so cost is understood before the build begins.

Bots follow the organization’s existing identity, data loss prevention, and access policies through Dataverse and Power Platform’s security model, so a bot never has broader access to data than the person using it would.
Conversations that fall outside the bot’s scope escalate to a human agent with the full conversation history attached, so the person does not have to repeat themselves.
Yes. A single bot build deploys consistently across Microsoft Teams, web and social channels, and voice, so behavior and answers stay the same no matter where the conversation starts.
Yes. Folio3 Azure reviews conversation analytics after go-live and folds new intents and phrasing back into the bot, so coverage and accuracy keep growing instead of freezing at launch.
